title: Russian drones strike a passenger train in Kharkiv Oblast
body:
On 27 January 2026, Russian drones struck a passenger train in the Barvinkove community of Kharkiv Oblast, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov. Prosecutors said three Geran-2 drones, the Russian designation for Shahed-type drones, were launched. One hit the train and two struck the area nearby. The blasts damaged the locomotive and a passenger car and started a fire.

Prosecutors initially reported at least five people killed and two injured. Kharkiv police chief Petro Tokar later said that six people had been killed. Ukrzaliznytsia, the state railway operator, and regional officials said the train was carrying 291 passengers. According to the Kyiv Independent, the service ran on the Barvinkove-Lviv-Chop route.

Emergency services, medics, rescuers and railway crews responded to the scene, and reserve buses were sent to transport passengers and people waiting for return trips. Deputy Prime Minister Oleksii Kuleba described the strike as a direct act of Russian terror against civilians and said there was no military target at the location. The attack took place during a winter in which Russian strikes on infrastructure, particularly energy facilities, were a major feature of the war.
